name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime
summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime is a serverless AWS hosting service that runs an agent's own code, written in any framework, in isolated sessions and serves it over HTTP, MCP, A2A or AG-UI.

skills.what: AWS's comparison of AgentCore harness and AgentCore Runtime marks Agent Skills as Custom on Runtime, meaning the agent's own code must load them; the separate AgentCore harness loads them by configuration.

mcp.what: AgentCore Runtime hosts MCP servers (Streamable HTTP at 0.0.0.0:8000/mcp) and AgentCore Gateway exposes tools as MCP endpoints, but connecting a Runtime agent to remote MCP servers is the agent's own code (marked Custom).

sources.title: Deploy MCP servers in AgentCore Runtime

plugins.what: Not found in Amazon Web Services' documentation.

hooks.what: AgentCore Runtime lifecycle hooks call an endpoint in the agent's container at set points, currently only the build warmup hook during create and update on platform version V2 microVMs; hooks in the agent loop are the agent's own code (marked Custom).

sources.title: Configure lifecycle hooks for AgentCore Runtime

a2a.what: AgentCore Runtime deploys and serves A2A servers (port 9000, Agent Card at /.well-known/agent-card.json), passing JSON-RPC payloads through unchanged.

sources.title: Deploy A2A servers in AgentCore Runtime

scheduled-work.what: Not found in Amazon Web Services' documentation.

sandboxes.what: AgentCore Code Interpreter runs agent-written code in isolated sandbox sessions, and each AgentCore Runtime session runs in its own dedicated microVM with isolated compute, memory and filesystem.

sources.title: Execute code and analyze data using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter
